name: TCAN332
full_name: 3.3V CAN transceiver with CAN FD (normal mode only)
description: 3.3 V CAN FD bus transceiver (physical layer), ISO 11898-2 compliant. It is the bus driver a CAN controller (MCP2518FD, an MCU CAN peripheral) needs to reach the wire: it converts the controller's single-ended TXD/RXD to the differential CANH/CANL bus and back. TCAN332 is the 'normal mode only' member of the TCAN33x family, so pins 5 and 8 are NC; the siblings put features there: TCAN330 (SHDN + silent), TCAN334 (SHDN + standby/wake), TCAN337 (fault + silent). The plain part is rated to 1 Mbps; the -G speed grade (TCAN332G) runs to 5 Mbps.

pins.name: TXD
pins.description: transmit data input from the CAN controller (drives the bus)

pins.name: RXD
pins.description: receive data output to the CAN controller

pins.name: NC
pins.description: not connected on TCAN332 (SHDN on TCAN330/334)

pins.name: NC
pins.description: not connected on TCAN332 (S/silent on TCAN330, STB on TCAN334, FAULT on TCAN337)

extra.can: CAN / CAN FD, ISO 11898-2; up to 1 Mbps (TCAN332), up to 5 Mbps (TCAN332G)
extra.modes: normal mode only - no shutdown or standby on TCAN332 (pins 5 and 8 are NC)
extra.logic: 3.3 V TXD/RXD (interfaces directly to 3.3 V MCUs)

typical_application: The bus-side half of a 3.3 V CAN node: an MCU or CAN controller (e.g. MCP2518FD) drives TXD and reads RXD, and the TCAN332 puts it on the differential bus via CANH/CANL. Terminate the bus with 120 ohm at both ends.
gotchas: NO standby or shutdown - pins 5 and 8 are NC; if you need low-power standby or silent mode use TCAN334/TCAN330 (same pinout, those pins become STB/S)
transceiver ONLY - it does not do CAN protocol; pair it with a controller (MCP2518FD, MCP2515, or an MCU CAN peripheral)
3.3 V part - do not feed it 5 V; TXD/RXD logic is 3.3 V
the -G suffix (TCAN332G) is the 5 Mbps data-rate grade; the plain TCAN332 is rated to 1 Mbps - match the grade to your CAN FD data phase
the bus needs 120 ohm termination at both physical ends; the transceiver does not provide it
